subject.title: Exact deployment identity and Product QA acceptance snapshot

semantics.desiredOutcome: Product QA can accept only an exact immutable deployment subject whose Frontend and Backend deployable identities, correctness-relevant configuration and observed runtime identities are pinned and independently verified, preserving the distinction between deployment publication, runtime observation and quality acceptance.
semantics.currentState: The delivered system includes Backend/QA application slices, the organization boundary, bounded domain execution, and mutation-current authoritative publication, but it does not provide exact Frontend/Backend deployable provenance, a DevOps DeploymentRelease, an immutable AcceptanceSnapshot, independent runtime-identity observation, or Product QA QualityAcceptance over one exact deployed product subject.

requiredBehaviors.statement: Accepted Frontend and Backend delivery outputs are linked through build provenance to exact immutable deployable artifact identities such as content digests rather than mutable tags or branch names.
DevOps publishes one immutable DeploymentRelease that binds exact deployable artifacts, target environment, correctness-relevant deployment/configuration identity and rollout/health evidence.

AcceptanceSnapshot is derived deterministically from one exact DeploymentRelease plus the current required product acceptance subjects and cannot be assembled by arbitrarily omitting or mixing required components.
Product QA execution binds the exact AcceptanceSnapshot and cannot rewrite the snapshot or substitute a different release component during verification.
Runtime identity is observed independently from the tested environment under an explicit verifier policy; DevOps or application self-report alone is not sufficient runtime truth.
Mixed, unknown or mismatched runtime revisions prevent a current quality acceptance unless an explicit acceptance policy permits the observed bounded set.

Deployment and acceptance currentness are revalidated before QA effects and again before authoritative QualityAcceptance publication so a changing environment cannot be accepted as the newer current release.
Historical DeploymentRelease, AcceptanceSnapshot, runtime observations and QualityAcceptance remain immutable and reconstructable after newer deployment subjects become current.

The complete provenance chain from accepted source delivery through build artifact, deployment release, acceptance snapshot, runtime observation and criterion evidence remains fresh-session resolvable.

invariants.statement: Source revision is not deployable artifact identity.
Mutable image tag or alias is not immutable deployment identity.
QA strategy success is not equivalent to QualityAcceptance ACCEPT.
A caller-selected subset of component refs cannot prove acceptance completeness.
Deployment change during the QA verification window cannot produce current acceptance for the newer release.
DevOps and Product QA remain separate authority domains for deployment publication and quality judgment.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Exact Frontend and Backend deployable identities are traceable from accepted delivery/build provenance into one immutable DeploymentRelease.
AcceptanceSnapshot deterministically pins the exact required components, release, acceptance criteria, environment and verifier policy without omission or cross-release substitution.
Independent runtime observation detects mismatch between expected and actually served component identity and prevents current acceptance.
A mixed old/new rollout is blocked or inconclusive by default rather than silently accepted.
Deployment change before QA starts invalidates the current verification target; deployment change during QA prevents current QualityAcceptance publication for the changed release.
Old snapshots and acceptances remain reconstructable historical evidence after a newer release becomes current.
A fresh consumer can trace source delivery to build provenance, exact deployable, DeploymentRelease, AcceptanceSnapshot, RuntimeObservation and QualityAcceptance without prior conversation state.

outOfScope.statement: Global ProductStateProjection, product completeness and objective-closure semantics.
Universal software-supply-chain framework or mandatory Sigstore/in-toto adoption.
Generic artifact-registry rewrite or environment-inventory platform.
Automatic remediation or product-owner decision policy.
